newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court approves surveillance for far right.
newsitem.headline: German court approves surveillance for far right.

text.p: A court ruled on Friday Germany's anti-extremist watchdog could use undercover methods to monitor the activities of the far-right Republican party.
The court in the northern town of Lueneburg ruled the regional branch of the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution could use cloak-and-dagger methods to keep tabs on the Republicans.
Germany's other regional states have already placed the Republicans under surveillance and Friday's ruling meant Lower Saxony could now join them, the regional interior ministry said.
The ruling would allow investigators to trail members, tap phones, intercept mail and permit them access to private papers including accounts.
The Republicans said they would appeal against the verdict, which they described as "incomprehensible". The court did not immediately issue the reasons for its verdict.
